items.title: Jimmy Cobb — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: The interviewee mentions 'Paul' multiple times, but context clearly identifies him as Paul Chambers ('Then you get to Paul [Chambers], which is another genius... We had a good time. We worked with Miles... The trio was so together... We made some records with Wes Montgomery.' and 'Philly Joe [Jones]

ctx.x: I just read a quote where you said something – that he was epileptic?

That only happened when he got to be a grown man. That didn’t happen through the first part of his life. I don’t know what that was that happened. He got – I think he claimed that happened maybe after Paul died, that he was – he liked Paul so much, he started – he used to drink a lot. He was in a place in Brooklyn where they thought he was a man. They thought he was a young man that could play the piano. He started out when he was maybe 12, 13 years old. He could play the piano. I think what they say is Wynton,…
Why do you think he was underrated?
